comments: Final ALLFRAME+TRIAL fit to 17 of 36 Cepheids with P>25 d. Dust, bright background and anomalous aperture corrections motivated a 0.15 mag photometric random term, producing the relatively large e_R.

Alternative Key Project fit to Saha et al. photometry. Four outliers were removed from their 25-star final set, leaving 21 Cepheids; the unweighted mean of the individual dereddened moduli was adopted.
There are no specific comments on the publication. Cepheid moduli are compiled and homogenized from earlier HST Key Project and independent studies. Previous author included it.

Uncorrected re-fit of 17 previously selected Cepheids using the Stetson WFPC2 zero point, Udalski OGLE-LMC PL relations and mu_LMC=18.45. The quoted error is internal; the paper does not assign a galaxy-specific systematic term.

Metallicity-corrected result for the same 17 Cepheids, adopting gamma_VI=-0.2 mag dex^-1 and the published field abundance. The correction raises the modulus by 0.150 mag without changing the quoted internal error.

Published Sandage/Saha HST photometry reanalyzed by the Key Project is refitted with the OGLE-LMC PL calibration. The random error includes PL scatter and reddening uncertainty; no metallicity correction is applied.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Table 4 mu_Z, using gamma=-0.2 mag dex^-1 relative to the LMC. Metallicity uncertainty is systematic and excluded from e_R.
Udalski et al. (1999) PL calibration shifted to mu_LMC=18.50. This solution is 0.12 mag shorter than the MF91 result and differs from the value adopted by Freedman et al. (2001).
Preferred modulus, obtained as a conservative average of the MF91 and Udalski solutions. The uncertainty was enlarged accordingly; no separate systematic error or metallicity correction is provided.
Madore & Freedman (1991) PL calibration. The error is mainly associated with observational scatter. Photometry is fainter than earlier reductions, likely because of the local-sky treatment.
Preferred near-solar-metallicity solution with low Vlim sensitivity (+0.06/-0.03 mag). The 369 entries in Table 6 are sosie associations and cannot be treated as distinct Cepheids.
Present-paper HIPPARCOS-calibrated PL solution. The quoted uncertainty is internal; the incompleteness correction is small for this galaxy.
Maximum-light LMC PL solution used as a consistency check. CTE corrected; no metallicity correction.
Representative mean-light result using the authors' OGLE LMC PL fit. CTE corrected but not metallicity corrected; the error is random only.
Representative FSG03 Galactic mean-light solution. CTE corrected but not metallicity corrected.
LMC mean-light solution with a +0.150 mag metallicity correction; the additive correction leaves e_R unchanged.
FSG03 Galactic result with a +0.076 mag metallicity correction relative to Galactic abundance.
Revised SN Ia-host distance using corrected WFPC2 photometry. Period-dependent metallicity corrections bring the uncorrected GC/LMC moduli of 30.41/30.19 mag to the same final value.
Direct archival HST/ACS-WFC measurement. I_TRGB=25.83+/-0.10 is reported as color-independent. Applying A_I=0.06 mag gives mu_0=29.82. The result is used to calibrate SN Ia luminosity.
Measurement error is 0.03 mag, with an additional 0.12 mag systematic. Internal RGB extinction is assumed negligible. The result exceeds previous TRGB estimates by 0.30-0.52 mag.
Combined NGC 4258+LMC blue-I solution from reprocessed HST/ACS outer-field photometry (R_GC>=4.3 arcmin). Error is random only; the common systematic is 0.057 mag.
Preferred color-corrected QT solution on the combined NGC 4258+LMC scale. QT gives a narrower TRGB edge response. Error is random only; systematic=0.057 mag.
Flagged as uncertain because crowding, distance and metallicity blur the TRGB. M_I=-4.0+/-0.2 is adopted and only foreground extinction is corrected. Use with caution.
